newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese hotel chain applies for court protection.
newsitem.headline: Japanese hotel chain applies for court protection.

text.p: Japanese hotel chain operator Hokke Club KK said on Monday that it had applied for court protection so it can reorganise its financial affairs.
Hokke Club, which operates 13 hotels in Japan and two overseas, said it has debts of 22.6 billion yen ($189 million).
The company said it would try to rebuild its business with help from Accor Asia Pacific Ltd, a unit of major French hotel operator Accor SA, which operates the Hotel Sofitel chain.
In a statement released on Monday, Accor Asia Pacific said it would provide assistance to Hokke Club, but gave no further details.
Hokke Club opened its first hotel in Kyoto in 1920 to provide accommodation for Buddhist pilgrims.
The firm, which operates low-priced hotels aimed at business executives, has faced a sharp drop in earnings since Japan's economy slumped in the early 1990s.
In addition to its hotels in Japan, it has one in India and another in Nepal.
The firm filed for protection from creditors under Japan's bankruptcy laws at Kyoto district court. ($1=119 yen)
